sentences.chinese: 郭默小丑，何足以勞公神略，可留征虜將軍貝丘王翼光守之，公其還也。
sentences.literal: Guo Mo is a petty rascal; how could he suffice to weary your divine strategy? You may leave General Who Strikes Down the Barbarians Wang Yiguang, Prince of Beiqu, to hold him; as for you, sir, you ought to return.
sentences.idiomatic: Guo Mo is a negligible foe—hardly worth straining your stratagem. Leave General Who Crushes the Barbarians Wang Yiguang of Beiqu to pin him in place and withdraw yourself.

sentences.chinese: 」於是曜歸薄阪。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon Yao returned to Puban.
sentences.idiomatic: When the message was delivered Liu Yao marched back to Puban.

sentences.chinese: 俄而徵曜輔政。
sentences.literal: Before long [the court] summoned Yao to aid in governing.
sentences.idiomatic: Soon afterward Liu Cong recalled Liu Yao to steer state affairs.

sentences.chinese: 趙染寇北地，夢魯徽大怒，引弓射之，染驚悸而寤。
sentences.literal: Zhao Ran raided Beidi; he dreamed that Lu Hui was greatly enraged, drew his bow, and shot him; Zhao Ran woke alarmed and trembling.
sentences.idiomatic: Raiding Beidi, Zhao Ran dreamed Lu Hui raging, bent a bow, and loosed a shaft at him—he jolted awake petrified.

sentences.chinese: 旦將攻城，中弩而死。
sentences.literal: When dawn came he was about to assault the city and was struck by a crossbow bolt and died.
sentences.idiomatic: At sunrise, on the point of scaling the walls, he caught a quarrel and fell dead.

sentences.chinese: 聰以粲為相國，總百揆，省丞相以並相國。
sentences.literal: Liu Cong appointed Liu Can Chancellor of State, superintended the hundred administrations, abolished the office of Chancellor, and consolidated its duties with the Chancellorship of State.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Cong installed Liu Can as chancellor of state atop every ministry, then abolished the old chancellor title so that authority pooled in that office alone.

sentences.chinese: 平陽地震，烈風拔樹髮屋。
sentences.literal: Pingyang shook in an earthquake; fierce winds uprooted trees and tore off roofs.
sentences.idiomatic: Quakes rocked Pingyang while gales uprooted timber and stripped roofs away.

sentences.chinese: 光義人羊充妻產子二頭，其兄竊而食之，三日而死。
sentences.literal: One Yang Chong's wife among the people of Guangyi gave birth to a two-headed infant; her elder brother stole it and ate it and died after three days.
sentences.idiomatic: In Guangyi commoner Yang Chong's wife bore a dicephalic child; her elder brother stole it, consumed it, and dropped dead three days later.

sentences.chinese: 聰以其太廟新成，大赦境內，改年建元。
sentences.literal: Liu Cong, because his dynastic Grand Temple was newly finished, declared a great amnesty within the borders and changed the reign period to Founding Yuan.
sentences.idiomatic: Celebrating the completion of his ancestral shrine, Liu Cong issued an empire-wide amnesty and adopted the Jiànyuan era.

sentences.chinese: 雨血於其東宮延明殿，徹瓦在地者深五寸。
sentences.literal: Blood rained upon his Eastern Palace Yanming Hall; where tiles had fallen to earth the depth reached five cun.
sentences.idiomatic: Crimson showers drenched Yanming Hall in the heir's precinct, pooling five cun deep over shattered tiles.

sentences.chinese: 劉乂惡之，以訪其太師盧志、太傅崔瑋、太保許遐。
sentences.literal: Liu Yi abhorred these things and consulted his grand preceptor Lu Zhi, grand tutor Cui Wei, and grand guardian Xu Xia.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Yi read the prodigies with dread and took counsel from Lu Zhi, Cui Wei, and Xu Xia.

sentences.chinese: 志等曰：「主上往以殿下為太弟者，蓋以安眾望也，志在晉王久矣，王公已下莫不希旨歸之。
sentences.literal: Lu Zhi and the others said: "The sovereign once named Your Highness heir apparent solely to placate widespread expectation; his purpose has leaned toward the Prince of Jin for ages, and none from royal dukes downward fails to read that intent and cling to him.
sentences.idiomatic: "The throne-maker made you heir only to soothe the court," they said; "his eye has rested on Liu Can for years, and every grandee follows that drift."

sentences.chinese: 相國之位，自魏武已來，非復人臣之官，主上本發明詔，置之為贈官，今忽以晉王居之，羽儀威尊逾于東宮，萬機之事無不由之，置太宰、大將軍及諸王之營以為羽翼，此事勢去矣，殿下不得立明也。
sentences.literal: Since the era of Wei Wu the Chancellorship of State has ceased to be a servant's commission; our lord issued an explicit rule treating it as a posthumously bestowed dignity. Suddenly the Prince of Jin fills it—the panoply of guards and ceremonial majesty outstrip the Eastern Palace, and none of the myriad policy threads bypass him. He has stationed the grand steward, the grand marshal, and the princes' military camps as wings. With power arrayed thus, momentum has slipped away—you cannot openly expect to ascend."
sentences.idiomatic: "Since Cao Cao the super-chancellorship overshadows mere ministers; your father barred living men from that title save as posthumous glory—yet Liu Can now occupies it with retinues grander than the crown prince's while every edict crosses his desk, flanked by steward, marshal, and royal hosts. Succession no longer visibly belongs to you."

sentences.chinese: 然非止不得立而已，不測之危厄在於旦夕，宜早為之所。
sentences.literal: Yet even failure to ascend is hardly the worst; immeasurable calamity threatens by every dawn—you must prepare early.
sentences.idiomatic: "Worse than losing the succession is imminent ruin—strike before catastrophe finds you."

sentences.chinese: 四衛精兵不減五千，余營諸王皆年齒尚幼，可奪而取之。
sentences.literal: The four guards' elite still number no fewer than five thousand; the other princes' encampments are led by youths—you can wrench them away.
sentences.idiomatic: The palace guard corps fields five thousand veterans, and child princes hold the outlying camps—both are there for the seizing.

sentences.chinese: 相國輕佻，正可煩一刺客耳。
sentences.literal: The Chancellor of State is rash; vexing yourself with armies is needless—a single dagger will do.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Can is reckless—hire one blade and remove him.

sentences.chinese: 大將軍無日不出，其營可襲而得也。
sentences.literal: The Grand Marshal exposes himself daily; ravage his lines and seize them outright.
sentences.idiomatic: The grand marshal rides out without fail—ambush his headquarters and overpower it.

sentences.chinese: 殿下但當有意，二萬精兵立便可得，鼓行向雲龍門，宿衛之士孰不倒戈奉迎，大司馬不慮為異也。
sentences.literal: Your Highness need only form the intent—twenty thousand picked soldiers may be gathered at once; beat drums toward the Yunlong Gate and which of the night-watch troops will not cast spears aside to hail you? The Grand Marshal should not presume to dissent.
sentences.idiomatic: Authorize the coup and twenty thousand veterans can march straight to Yunlong Gate, where night sentinels will gladly switch sides; the grand marshal will not obstruct you.

sentences.chinese: 」乂弗從，乃止。
sentences.literal: " Liu Yi would not heed them, and they desisted.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Yi refused, and the plot collapsed.

sentences.chinese: 聰如中護軍靳准第，納其二女為左右貴嬪，大曰月光，小曰月華，皆國色也。
sentences.literal: Liu Cong went to Chief Commandant of the Guards Jin Zhun's residence, took his two daughters as left and right Honored Concubines, the elder titled Moon Gleam, the younger Moon Bloom; both were beauties of national renown.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Cong visited Jin Zhun's mansion and inducted his daughters as left and right “noble beauties,” the elder Lady Moon Gleam and the younger Lady Moon Bloom, women famed through the realm.

sentences.chinese: 數月，立月光為皇后。
sentences.literal: Several months later he established Moon Gleam as Empress.
sentences.idiomatic: Within months Lady Moon Gleam was elevated to empress.

sentences.chinese: 東宮舍人荀裕告盧志等勸乂謀反，乂不從之狀。
sentences.literal: Eastern Palace steward Xun Yu reported the circumstance of Lu Zhi and others exhorting Liu Yi to rebel and Liu Yi refusing to follow.
sentences.idiomatic: Xun Yu, an aide in the heir's household, denounced Lu Zhi's circle for urging revolt on Liu Yi—counsel Yi had rejected.

sentences.chinese: 聰於是收志、瑋、遐於詔獄，假以他事殺之。
sentences.literal: Thereupon Liu Cong arrested Lu Zhi, Cui Wei, and Xu Xia in a prison opened by edict and, under other pretexts, executed them.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Cong jailed Lu Zhi, Cui Wei, and Xu Xia on manufactured charges and put them to death.

sentences.chinese: 使冠威卜抽監守東宮，禁乂朝賀。
sentences.literal: He ordered Guanwei Bu Chou to supervise and guard the Eastern Palace and forbade Liu Yi from attending court congratulations.
sentences.idiomatic: He posted Bu Chou, colonel of the crown guards, on the heir's mansion and barred Liu Yi from court felicitations.

sentences.chinese: 乂憂懼不知所為，乃上表自陳，乞為黔首，並免諸子之封，褒美晉王粲宜登儲副，抽又抑而弗通。
sentences.literal: Yi, anxious and afraid, not knowing what to do, submitted a memorial stating himself, begging to become a black-haired commoner, together canceling enfeoffments for all his sons, extolling the Prince of Jin Can as fit to rise to the secondary heir—Draw moreover suppressed it and did not transmit it.
sentences.idiomatic: Panicking, Liu Yi offered to become a commoner, strip his sons of titles, and praise Liu Can as successor—Bu Draw buried the petition.

sentences.chinese: 其青州刺史曹嶷攻汶陽關、公丘，陷之，害齊郡太守徐浮，執建威劉宣，齊魯之間郡縣壘壁降者四十餘所。
sentences.literal: His governor of Qingzhou Cao Yi attacked Wenyang Pass and Gongqiu, overran them, killed Grand Administrator of Qi Commandery Xu Fu, captured General Who Establishes Might Liu Xuan, and between Qi and Lu more than forty county seats and fortresses surrendered.
sentences.idiomatic: Cao Yi of Qingzhou stormed Wenyang barrier and Gongqiu, slew Qi prefect Xu Fu, took Liu Xuan captive, and brought over forty citadels between Qi and Lu to heel.

sentences.chinese: 嶷遂略地，西下祝阿、平陰，眾十餘萬，臨河置戍，而歸於臨淄。
sentences.literal: Cao Yi thereupon extended his territory, marched west to capture Zhu'a and Pingyin, massed more than a hundred thousand men, posted river garrisons, and returned to Linzi.
sentences.idiomatic: He swept west through Zhu'a and Pingyin, raised above a hundred thousand warriors, seeded pickets along the Yellow River, and pulled back toward Linzi.

sentences.chinese: 嶷於是遂雄據全齊之志。
sentences.literal: Cao Yi thereupon conceived the ambition of heroically dominating the whole of Qi.
sentences.idiomatic: From there Cao Yi intended to make himself master of all Qi.

sentences.chinese: 石勒以嶷之懷二也，請討之。
sentences.literal: Shi Le, because Cao Yi nursed duplicity, requested permission to campaign against him.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Le, scenting disloyalty in Cao Yi, asked to crush him.

sentences.chinese: 聰又憚勒之並齊，乃寢而弗許。
sentences.literal: Liu Cong again feared Shi Le's annexation of Qi, and therefore tabled the matter and did not grant approval.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Cong, afraid Shi Le would swallow Shandong, shelved the request.

sentences.chinese: 劉曜濟自盟津，將攻河南，將軍魏該奔於一泉塢。
sentences.literal: Liu Yao crossed at Meng Ford intending to attack Henan; General Wei Gai fled to Yiquan stockade.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Yao forded Mengjin to overrun Henan while commander Wei Gai escaped to the Yiquan redoubt.

sentences.chinese: 曜進攻李矩于滎陽，矩遣將軍李平師于成皋，曜覆而滅之。
sentences.literal: Yao advanced to attack Li Ju at Yingyang; Ju sent General Li Ping, who encamped at Chenggao; Yao enveloped and destroyed him.
sentences.idiomatic: Besieging Li Ju at Yingyang, Liu Yao crushed Li Ping's Chenggao camp in a envelopment.

sentences.chinese: 矩恐，送質請降。
sentences.literal: Ju, frightened, sent hostages begging to surrender.
sentences.idiomatic: Terror-struck, Li Ju forwarded hostages to sue for terms.

sentences.chinese: 時聰以其皇后靳氏為上皇后，立貴妃劉氏為左皇后，右貴嬪靳氏為右皇后。
sentences.literal: At the time Liu Cong took his Empress Lady Jin as Senior Empress, established Honored Concubine Lady Liu as Left Empress, and Right Honored Concubine Lady Jin as Right Empress.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Cong simultaneously enthroned Empress Jin as “chief empress,” a Lady Liu as left empress, and a second Lady Jin as right empress.

sentences.chinese: 左司隸陳元達以三后之立也，極諫，聰不納，乃以元達為右光祿大夫，外示優賢，內實奪其權也。
sentences.literal: Left Metropolitan Commandant Chen Yuanda, over the establishment of three empresses, remonstrated to the utmost; Liu Cong did not accept it, and therefore made Yuanda Right Grand Master of Brilliant Splendor, outwardly displaying favor to worthies while inwardly stripping his authority.
sentences.idiomatic: Chen Yuanda protested the triple queens in vain; Liu Cong “promoted” him to Right Grand Master of Brilliant Splendor—a hollow honour that severed his power.

sentences.chinese: 於是太尉范隆、大司馬劉丹、大司空呼延晏、尚書令王鑒等皆抗表遜位，以讓元達。
sentences.literal: Thereupon Defender-in-chief Fan Long, Grand Marshal Liu Dan, Minister of Works Huyan Yan, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian, and others all submitted memorials declining office to yield to Yuanda.
sentences.idiomatic: Fan Long, Liu Dan, Huyan Yan, Wang Jian, and others resigned in concert to force Chen Yuanda's reinstatement.

sentences.chinese: 聰乃以元達為御史大夫、儀同三司。
sentences.literal: Liu Cong thereupon appointed Yuanda Censor-in-chief with peer standing of the Three Offices.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Cong relented, naming Chen Yuanda chief censor with Three-Duke protocol.

sentences.chinese: 劉曜寇長安，頻為王師所敗。
sentences.literal: Liu Yao raided Chang'an and was repeatedly defeated by the royal army.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Yao struck at Chang'an but Jin troops drove him back again and again.

sentences.chinese: 曜曰：「彼猶強盛，弗可圖矣。
sentences.literal: Yao said: "They remain strong; they cannot be schemed against.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Yao judged, “The enemy is still too mighty to overthrow.”

sentences.chinese: 」引師而歸。
sentences.literal: " He led the army back.
sentences.idiomatic: He broke off and withdrew.

sentences.chinese: 聰宮中鬼夜哭，三日而聲向右司隸寺，乃止。
sentences.literal: In Liu Cong's palace ghosts wept by night; after three days the sound shifted to the right metropolitan commandant's office, then ceased.
sentences.idiomatic: Spectral wailing haunted Liu Cong's harem for three nights before migrating to the right metropolitan jail and dying away.

sentences.chinese: 其上皇后靳氏有淫穢之行，陳元達奏之。
sentences.literal: His Senior Empress Lady Jin had conduct of lewdness; Chen Yuanda memorialized it.
sentences.idiomatic: Chief empress Jin was caught in debauchery; Chen Yuanda impeached her.

sentences.chinese: 聰廢靳，靳慚恚自殺。
sentences.literal: Liu Cong deposed Jin; Jin, ashamed and enraged, committed suicide.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Cong cast her aside; distraught with shame, she took her life.

sentences.chinese: 靳有殊寵，聰迫于元達之勢，故廢之。
sentences.literal: Jin had enjoyed extraordinary favour; Liu Cong, pressured by Yuanda's influence, therefore deposed her.
sentences.idiomatic: She had been Liu Cong's favourite, yet he discarded her beneath Chen Yuanda's moral sway.

sentences.chinese: 既而追念其姿色，深仇元達。
sentences.literal: Afterwards he recalled her beauty and nursed bitter hatred toward Yuanda.
sentences.idiomatic: Soon he brooded on her charms and harboured deep resentment against Chen Yuanda.

sentences.chinese: 劉曜進師上黨，將攻陽曲，聰遣使謂曜曰：「長安擅命，國家之深恥也。
sentences.literal: Liu Yao advanced troops to Shangdang intending to attack Yangqu; Liu Cong dispatched messengers telling Yao: "Chang'an's arrogant assumption of mandate is our dynasty's profound shame.
sentences.idiomatic: Marching from Shangdang on Yangqu, Liu Yao received Liu Cong's order: “Jin's grip on Chang'an shames us most.”

sentences.chinese: 公宜以長安為先，陽曲一委驃騎。
sentences.literal: You ought to place Chang'an first; leave Yangqu entirely to the Cavalry-in-ordinary.
sentences.idiomatic: Strike Chang'an first and leave Yangqu wholly to your cavalry marshal.

sentences.chinese: 天時人事，其應至矣，公其亟還。
sentences.literal: Heaven's seasons and human affairs—their convergence has arrived; you, sir, should hurry back.
sentences.idiomatic: Heaven and men both align—return without delay.

sentences.chinese: 」曜回滅郭邁，朝於聰，遂如蒲阪。
sentences.literal: " Yao wheeled about, extinguished Guo Mai, had audience with Liu Cong, and proceeded to Puban.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Yao swung his host, wiped out Guo Mai, paid homage at Pingyang, and moved on to Puban.

sentences.chinese: 平陽地震，雨血於東宮，廣袤頃餘。
sentences.literal: Pingyang shook in an earthquake; blood rained on the Eastern Palace covering more than a qing.
sentences.idiomatic: Another temblor hit Pingyang while gore showered the heir's compound across over a qing of ground.

sentences.chinese: 劉曜又進軍，屯於粟邑。
sentences.literal: Liu Yao again advanced the army and encamped at Suiyi.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Yao pushed forward again and camped at Suiyi.

sentences.chinese: 麹允饑甚，去黃白而軍于靈武。
sentences.literal: Qu Yun was exceedingly famished; he abandoned Huangbai and encamped at Lingwu.
sentences.idiomatic: Qu Yun, starving, quit the Huangbai stronghold for Lingwu.

sentences.chinese: 曜進攻上郡，太守張禹與馮翊太守梁肅奔於允吾。
sentences.literal: Yao attacked Shang Commandery; Grand Administrator Zhang Yu with Grand Administrator of Fengyi Liang Su fled to Yunwu.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Yao stormed Shang—prefect Zhang Yu fled with Fengyi's Liang Su toward Yunwu.

sentences.chinese: 於是關右翕然，所在應曜。
sentences.literal: Thereupon west of the passes all murmured assent; everywhere they answered Yao.
sentences.idiomatic: Northwest of Tong Pass the country murmured and rose to Liu Yao's call.

sentences.chinese: 曜進據黃阜。
sentences.literal: Yao advanced and occupied Huangfu.
sentences.idiomatic: He seized the Huangfu heights.

sentences.chinese: 聰武庫陷入地一丈五尺。
sentences.literal: Liu Cong's armoury sank into earth one zhang five chi deep.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Cong's arsenal yard subsided fifteen chi into the soil.

sentences.chinese: 時聰中常侍王沈、宣懷、俞容，中宮僕射郭猗，中黃門陵修等皆寵倖用事。
sentences.literal: At the time Liu Cong's palace attendants Wang Shen, Xuan Huai, and Yu Rong, Central Palace Supervisor Guo Yi, and Yellow Gate Ling Xiu and others were all favoured favourites wielding affairs.
sentences.idiomatic: Eunuch favourites—Wang Shen, Xuan Huai, Yu Rong, Guo Yi the inner-palace steward, Ling Xiu of the Yellow Gate, and their ilk—ran the regime.

sentences.chinese: 聰游宴後宮，或百日不出，群臣皆因沈等言事，多不呈聰，率以其意愛憎而決之，故或有勳舊功臣而弗見敘錄，奸佞小人數日而便至二千石者。
sentences.literal: Liu Cong roved and banqueted in the rear palaces; sometimes a hundred days without emerging; all officials relayed business through Shen and company, much of which never reached Liu Cong; broadly they resolved matters by their personal loves and hates—hence sometimes meritorious old ministers went unrecorded while sycophantic petty men reached two-thousand-shi rank within days.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Cong caroused behind vermilion walls for months on end while ministers routed paperwork through Wang Shen's clique—seldom reaching the throne—so favours alone decided posts, skipping venerable heroes while toadies jumped to fat salaries overnight.

sentences.chinese: 軍旅無歲不興，而將士無錢帛之賞，後宮之家賜齎及於僮僕，動至數千萬。
sentences.literal: Armies marched every year yet commanders received no grants of coin or silk; households of the rear palaces were gifted to the point of servants and pages, routinely reaching tens of millions.
sentences.idiomatic: Campaigns never ceased, yet troops went unpaid; imperial concubines showered slaves with gifts running into tens of millions of cash.

sentences.chinese: 沈等車服宅宇皆逾于諸王，子弟、中表布衣為內史令長者三十餘人，皆奢僭貪殘，賊害良善。
sentences.literal: Shen and company—carriages, robes, dwellings, all exceeded those of the princes; more than thirty of their sons and cousins-by-marriage became commoners appointed commandery administrators or magistrates, all extravagant, overweening, greedy, cruel, looting and killing the good.
sentences.idiomatic: Wang Shen's cabal flaunted carriages and mansions finer than princes', placing thirty-plus kinsmen as local magistrates—luxury-mad plunderers one and all.

sentences.chinese: 靳准合宗內外諂以事之。
sentences.literal: Jin Zhun assembled his whole clan inside and outside to flatter and serve them.
sentences.idiomatic: Jin Zhun rallied his entire kin to curry favour with them.

sentences.chinese: 郭猗有憾于劉乂，謂劉粲曰：「太弟于主上之世猶懷不逞之志，此則殿下父子之深仇，四海蒼生之重怨也。
sentences.literal: Guo Yi nursed a grudge toward Liu Yi and said to Liu Can: "During the Sovereign's lifetime the heir-apparent brother still harbors unbridled ambitions—this is deep enmity between Your Highness and your father as well as the heavy resentment of all within the four seas.
sentences.idiomatic: Guo Yi, nursing spite against Liu Yi, whispered to Liu Can, “While your father yet rules, your uncle the heir cherishes ambitions that make you mortal enemies and turn the realm against him.”

sentences.chinese: 而主上過垂寬仁，猶不替二尊之位，一旦有風塵之變，臣竊為殿下寒心。
sentences.literal: Yet the Sovereign has been excessively lenient and still does not remove the two exalted seats; once storm winds of change arise, your servant secretly shivers for Your Highness.
sentences.idiomatic: “Yet the emperor indulges him and leaves both thrones untouched—when crisis breaks you will suffer first.”

sentences.chinese: 且殿下高祖之世孫，主上之嫡統，凡在含齒，孰不系仰。
sentences.literal: Moreover Your Highness is the great-grandson of Gaozu and the Sovereign's legitimate line—whoever bears teeth fails to hang his hopes on you.
sentences.idiomatic: “You alone are Gaozu's great-grandson and the true imperial line—every citizen looks to you.”

sentences.chinese: 萬機事大，何可與人！
sentences.literal: The myriad handles are too great—how may they be shared with another!
sentences.idiomatic: “The purple business is not for sharing.”

sentences.chinese: 臣昨聞太弟與大將軍相見，極有言矣，若事成，許以主上為在太上皇，大將軍為皇太子。
sentences.literal: Yesterday I heard the heir-apparent brother and the Grand Marshal met and held deep talks; should the enterprise succeed they pledged to reset the Sovereign as Retired August Throne-holder and install the Grand Marshal as crown prince.
sentences.idiomatic: “Yesterday your uncle huddled with the grand marshal; if they win they plan to pension the Son of Heaven as 'supreme father' and crown the marshal heir.”

sentences.chinese: 乂又許衛軍為大單于，二王已許之矣。
sentences.literal: Liu Yi moreover promised the Guards-general the Great Chanyu; the two royal lords have already assented.
sentences.idiomatic: “They even promised the guard-general the title of grand chanyu—both princes agreed.”

sentences.chinese: 二王居不疑之地，並握重兵，以此舉事，事何不成！
sentences.literal: The two royal lords sit in unquestioned stations and jointly grip heavy armies—undertaking affairs on this footing, how can the matter fail!
sentences.idiomatic: “Each holds unquestioned rank and veteran legions—their plot cannot miss.”

sentences.chinese: 臣謂二王茲舉，禽獸之不若也。
sentences.literal: Your servant holds that for this action of the two royal lords not even beasts would be their match.
sentences.idiomatic: “Their scheme is viler than beasts.”

sentences.chinese: 背父親人，人豈親之！
sentences.literal: Those who turn their backs on fathers and kin—how should others treat them as kin!
sentences.idiomatic: “Men who sell out father and brother win no loyalty.”

sentences.chinese: 今又苟貪其一切之力耳，事成之後，主上豈有全理！
sentences.literal: Now they moreover greedily grasp at momentary force; once the deed is done, how should the Sovereign remain whole in principle!
sentences.idiomatic: “They only covet raw power; once enthroned they will never spare your father.”

sentences.chinese: 殿下兄弟故在忘言，東宮、相國、單于在武陵兄弟，何肯與人！
sentences.literal: Your Highness and your brothers remain in relations where words are forgotten; the Eastern Palace, Chancellor of State, and Chanyu are Wuling-style brothers—how would they hand [power] to another!
sentences.idiomatic: “You still trust fraternal bonds, but heir, chancellor, and chanyu are a Wuling clique—they will never yield the realm.”

sentences.chinese: 許以三月上巳因宴作難，事淹變生，宜早為之所。
sentences.literal: They pledged on the third month's upper-si festival to raise trouble at a banquet; delay lets schemes shift—you must act early.
sentences.idiomatic: “They fixed the spring Shangsi banquet for the coup—hesitation invites disaster.”

sentences.chinese: 《春秋傳》曰：'蔓草猶不可除，況君之寵弟乎！
sentences.literal: The Zuo Commentary says: 'Even rampant weeds cannot be eradicated—how much less a sovereign's cherished younger brother!'
sentences.idiomatic: The Zuo warns: 'Runaway grass defies rooting out—let alone a ruler's pet brother.'

sentences.chinese: '臣屢啟主上，主上性敦友于，謂臣言不實。
sentences.literal: ' Your servant has repeatedly opened his heart to the Sovereign; the Sovereign's nature esteems fraternal duty and deems your servant's words untrue.
sentences.idiomatic: “I have warned the throne, but his nature clings to brotherly piety and dismisses me.”

sentences.chinese: 刑臣刀鋸之余，而蒙主上、殿下成造之恩，故不慮逆鱗之誅，每所聞必言，冀垂採納。
sentences.literal: As the leavings of knife and saw, I yet received the nurturing grace of Sovereign and Your Highness; therefore I do not fear execution for touching the inverse scales—whatever I hear I must speak, hoping you will deign to accept.
sentences.idiomatic: “A mutilated retainer whom you both favoured, I still risk regicide talk so you might listen.”

sentences.chinese: 臣當入言之。
sentences.literal: Your servant will enter and speak of it.
sentences.idiomatic: “I shall raise it with the emperor again.”

sentences.chinese: 願殿下不泄，密表其狀也。
sentences.literal: May Your Highness not leak word; secretly memorialize the circumstances.
sentences.idiomatic: “Say nothing outwardly—submit a sealed brief instead.”

sentences.chinese: 若不信臣言，可呼大將軍從事中郎王皮、衛軍司馬劉惇，假之恩顧，通其歸善之路以問之，必可知也。
sentences.literal: If you do not trust your servant's words, summon the Grand Marshal's registrar Wang Pi and the Guard-general's major Liu Dun, grant them gracious regard, open a path that they may return to loyalty, and question them—you can know for certain.
sentences.idiomatic: “If you doubt me, coax Wang Pi and Liu Dun with favours—they will confess.”

sentences.chinese: 」粲深然之。
sentences.literal: " Liu Can fully assented.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Can believed every word.

sentences.chinese: 猗密謂皮、惇曰：「二王逆狀，主、相已具知之矣，卿同之乎？
sentences.literal: Guo Yi secretly told Pi and Dun: "The treason of the two royal lords—Sovereign and Chancellor already fully know of it; do you concur?
sentences.idiomatic: Guo Yi cornered Wang Pi and Liu Dun: “The Son of Heaven and Liu Can already know your princes’ treason—do you?”

sentences.chinese: 」二人驚曰？
sentences.literal: " The two men cried out in alarm?!
sentences.idiomatic: The pair gasped.

sentences.chinese: ：「無之。
sentences.literal: : "There is nothing of it.
sentences.idiomatic: They stammered there was no plot.

sentences.chinese: 」猗曰：「此事必無疑，吾憐卿親舊並見族耳。
sentences.literal: " Guo Yi said: "In this matter there is no doubt; I pity you that kin and old friends will be exterminated wholesale.
sentences.idiomatic: “Deny it and your clans burn,” Guo Yi warned.

sentences.chinese: 」於是歔欷流涕。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon they sobbed and shed tears.
sentences.idiomatic: He wept theatrically.

sentences.chinese: 皮、惇大懼，叩頭求哀。
sentences.literal: Pi and Dun were greatly frightened, kowtowed begging mercy.
sentences.idiomatic: They fell prostrate, pleading for their lives.

sentences.chinese: 猗曰：「吾為卿作計，卿能用不？
sentences.literal: " Guo Yi said: "I will devise a plan for you—can you employ it?
sentences.idiomatic: “I can save you—will you obey?”

sentences.chinese: 」二人皆曰：「謹奉大人之教。
sentences.literal: " The two both said: "We respectfully receive the great man's teaching.
sentences.idiomatic: “Command us,” they said.

sentences.chinese: 」猗曰：「相國必問卿，卿但云有之。
sentences.literal: " Guo Yi said: "The Chancellor of State is sure to question you; you need only answer that it is so.
sentences.idiomatic: “When Liu Can asks, admit the plot.”

sentences.chinese: 若責卿何不先啟，卿即答云：'臣誠負死罪，然仰惟主上聖性寬慈，殿下篤于骨肉，恐言成詿偽故也。
sentences.literal: If he reproaches you for why you did not report first, you immediately answer: 'Your servant indeed deserves death, yet looking up I considered the Sovereign's sacred nature magnanimous and Your Highness's devotion to flesh and bone, fearing speech would become slander—hence [silence].
sentences.idiomatic: “If he demands why you stayed silent, say you dreaded false witness against a loving father and son.”

sentences.chinese: '」皮、惇許諾。
sentences.literal: '" Pi and Dun promised.
sentences.idiomatic: They swore to the script.

sentences.chinese: 粲俄而召問二人，至不同時，而辭若畫一，粲以為信然。
sentences.literal: Liu Can shortly thereafter summoned and questioned the two men; arriving at non-identical moments, their wording matched as though drawn with one template—Liu Can believed it true.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Can grilled them separately; their stories matched line for line, so he trusted the fraud.

sentences.chinese: 初，靳准從妹為乂孺子，淫于侍人，乂怒殺之，而屢以嘲准。
sentences.literal: Initially Jin Zhun's cousin by marriage had become Liu Yi's concubine; she committed lewdness with attendants; Liu Yi in anger killed her and repeatedly used the matter to mock Zhun.
sentences.idiomatic: Long before, Jin Zhun's cousin had entered Liu Yi's harem, dallied with pages, and died at Yi's hand—an episode Jin Zhun never forgave.

sentences.chinese: 准深慚恚，說粲曰：「東宮萬機之副，殿下宜自居之，以領相國，使天下知早有所系望也。
sentences.literal: Zhun deeply resented it and said to Liu Can: "The Eastern Palace is lieutenant to the myriad handles; Your Highness ought yourself to occupy it and superintend the Chancellor of State, letting the realm know early where hopes are fixed.
sentences.idiomatic: Jin Zhun urged Liu Can to seize the Eastern Palace and oversee the chancellorship so the world saw where power lay.

sentences.chinese: 」至是，准又說粲曰：「昔孝成距子政之言，使王氏卒成篡逆，可乎？
sentences.literal: At this point Zhun again said to Liu Can: "Formerly Emperor Cheng rejected Zizheng's counsel and allowed the Wang clan finally to usurp—was that acceptable?
sentences.idiomatic: He added, “Emperor Cheng spurned Liu Xiang and let the Wangs usurp—will you repeat it?”

sentences.chinese: 」粲曰：「何可之有！
sentences.literal: " Liu Can said: "How could it be acceptable!
sentences.idiomatic: “Never,” said Liu Can.

sentences.chinese: 」准曰：「然，誠如聖旨。
sentences.literal: " Zhun said: "Indeed; it is truly as the sagely decree.
sentences.idiomatic: “Then hear me,” Jin Zhun pressed.

sentences.chinese: 下官亟欲有所言矣，但以德非更生，親非皇宗，恐忠言暫出，霜威已及，故不敢耳。
sentences.literal: Your humble official has long wished to speak, but because my virtue is not that of Gengsheng and my kinship is not imperial stock, I feared loyal words would hardly leave my mouth before frost-like wrath arrived—therefore I dared not.
sentences.idiomatic: “I would have spoken sooner, but lacking Liu Xiang's virtue and royal blood I feared instant death—until now.”

sentences.chinese: 」粲曰：「君但言之。
sentences.literal: " Liu Can said: "You need only speak.
sentences.idiomatic: “Speak freely,” Liu Can said.

sentences.chinese: 」准曰：「聞風塵之言，謂大將軍、衛將軍及左右輔皆謀奉太弟，克季春構變，殿下宜為之備。
sentences.literal: " Zhun said: "Rumour on the wind says the Grand Marshal, Guard-general, and left and right assistants all plot to enthrone the heir-apparent brother, will complete the mutiny in late spring—Your Highness ought to prepare.
sentences.idiomatic: Jin Zhun closed: “Word says the marshal, guard-general, and aides mean to crown your uncle this spring—arm yourself.”
